vignette: A school-age child presents shortly after a fall with a fractured maxillary central incisor that has an immature root and an exposed pulp. The child is otherwise healthy.
stem: Which principle best guides the management of the pulp in this tooth?

options.text: Pulp preservation is mainly intended for fully formed teeth, so the pulp here should be removed at the outset.
The pulp should be preserved, because this allows root development and apex formation to continue.
The exposed immature pulp has little healing capacity, so pulp-preserving treatment is unlikely to succeed.
Keeping the pulp vital matters less in an immature tooth than in a mature tooth.
